text: In April 2015, a massive magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck $\textbf{Nepal}$, causing avalanches on $\textbf{Mount Everest}$ and destroying historical sites in $\textbf{Kathmandu}$.
explanation: The Gorkha earthquake was the worst natural disaster to strike Nepal since 1934, triggered by the collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates.

text: The $\textbf{Paris Agreement}$, a landmark global accord to combat $\textbf{Climate Change}$, was adopted at the $\textbf{COP21}$ summit held in $\textbf{France}$ in December 2015.
explanation: The agreement aims to limit global warming to well below 2, preferably to 1.5 degrees Celsius, compared to pre-industrial levels.

text: The $\textbf{New Suez Canal}$, a massive expansion project to allow two-way traffic and reduce transit time, was officially opened by $\textbf{Egypt}$ in August 2015.
explanation: The expansion added a new 35km shipping lane alongside the existing canal, significantly increasing its capacity.

text: Hurricane $\textbf{Patricia}$ became the most intense tropical cyclone on record in the $\textbf{Western Hemisphere}$ in October 2015 before making landfall in $\textbf{Mexico}$.
explanation: Patricia reached wind speeds of 215 mph (345 km/h) off the Pacific coast of Mexico.

text: In 2015, $\textbf{China}$ announced the end of its decades-long $\textbf{One-Child Policy}$, allowing all couples to have $\textbf{Two Children}$ to combat an aging population.
explanation: This major demographic shift was a response to a shrinking workforce and gender imbalance.

text: The NASA probe $\textbf{New Horizons}$ performed the first-ever flyby of $\textbf{Pluto}$ in July 2015, revealing complex geography including nitrogen ice $\textbf{Glaciers}$.
explanation: The mission provided the first close-up images of the dwarf planet and its moon Charon, located in the Kuiper Belt.

text: The $\textbf{European Migrant Crisis}$ peaked in 2015, with over a million refugees crossing the $\textbf{Mediterranean Sea}$ to reach countries like $\textbf{Germany}$ and $\textbf{Sweden}$.
explanation: Many refugees were fleeing the civil war in Syria, crossing from Turkey to Greece or from Libya to Italy.

text: The $\textbf{Calbuco}$ volcano in $\textbf{Chile}$ erupted unexpectedly in 2015 after 43 years of dormancy, forcing the evacuation of the $\textbf{Los Lagos}$ region.
explanation: Chile is located on the Pacific Ring of Fire and has the second-largest chain of active volcanoes in the world.

text: Cyclone $\textbf{Pam}$ caused widespread devastation in the Pacific island nation of $\textbf{Vanuatu}$ in March 2015, destroying infrastructure in the capital, $\textbf{Port Vila}$.
explanation: It was one of the most intense tropical cyclones ever recorded in the South Pacific Ocean.

text: In 2015, $\textbf{Lake Poopó}$, formerly $\textbf{Bolivia}$'s second-largest lake, was declared officially dried up due to climate change and water diversion.
explanation: The disappearance of the lake was a major ecological disaster for the Altiplano region.

text: The $\textbf{Milan Expo 2015}$ was held in $\textbf{Italy}$ with the theme 'Feeding the Planet, Energy for Life', focusing on $\textbf{Food Security}$ and sustainability.
explanation: The World Expo brought together 145 participating countries to showcase technologies for a sustainable future.

text: NASA announced in 2015 that liquid $\textbf{Water}$ flows intermittently on present-day $\textbf{Mars}$, creating dark streaks called $\textbf{Recurring Slope Lineae}$.
explanation: This discovery significantly impacted the search for potential life on the Red Planet.

text: The civil war in $\textbf{Yemen}$ escalated in 2015, threatening the strategic $\textbf{Bab el-Mandeb}$ strait which connects the $\textbf{Red Sea}$ to the Gulf of Aden.
explanation: This strait is a crucial chokepoint for global oil shipments and maritime trade.

text: The $\textbf{Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP)}$ trade agreement was agreed upon by 12 $\textbf{Pacific Rim}$ countries in 2015, excluding $\textbf{China}$.
explanation: The massive trade deal aimed to deepen economic ties among nations bordering the Pacific Ocean.

text: A massive $\textbf{El Niño}$ event began in 2015, causing extreme weather patterns globally, including droughts in $\textbf{Ethiopia}$ and floods in $\textbf{Paraguay}$.
explanation: The 2015-2016 El Niño was one of the strongest on record, significantly raising global temperatures.

text: A magnitude 6.0 earthquake struck near $\textbf{Mount Kinabalu}$ in $\textbf{Malaysia}$ in 2015, causing rockfalls on the country's highest peak.
explanation: Mount Kinabalu is located in the state of Sabah on the island of Borneo.

text: In September 2015, $\textbf{Queen Elizabeth II}$ became the longest-reigning monarch in $\textbf{British}$ history, surpassing Queen Victoria.
explanation: Her reign began in 1952, witnessing vast changes in the geography of the Commonwealth.

text: Tensions rose in the $\textbf{South China Sea}$ in 2015 as $\textbf{China}$ accelerated the construction of $\textbf{Artificial Islands}$ in the Spratly archipelago.
explanation: The reclamation projects raised concerns about freedom of navigation in the disputed waters.

text: A severe $\textbf{Heatwave}$ struck $\textbf{India}$ and $\textbf{Pakistan}$ in May 2015, claiming thousands of lives due to extreme temperatures.
explanation: Temperatures exceeded 47°C (117°F), highlighting the region's vulnerability to climate extremes.

text: In 2015, the $\textbf{World Health Organization}$ declared $\textbf{Sierra Leone}$ free of $\textbf{Ebola}$, marking a turning point in the West African epidemic.
explanation: The outbreak had severely impacted the geography and economy of Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.

text: The $\textbf{Danakil Depression}$ in $\textbf{Ethiopia}$ is often cited as the hottest inhabited place on Earth, featuring sulfur springs and salt plains.
explanation: It lies at the junction of three tectonic plates in the Horn of Africa.

text: The $\textbf{Bering Strait}$ separates the $\textbf{Seward Peninsula}$ of Alaska from the $\textbf{Chukchi Peninsula}$ of Russia.
explanation: This strait connects the Pacific Ocean (Bering Sea) to the Arctic Ocean (Chukchi Sea).

text: The $\textbf{Great Barrier Reef}$ off the coast of $\textbf{Australia}$ is the world's largest coral reef system, visible from space.
explanation: It stretches for over 2,300 kilometers along the coast of Queensland.

text: The $\textbf{McMurdo Dry Valleys}$ are a row of snow-free valleys in $\textbf{Antarctica}$, known for being one of the world's most extreme $\textbf{Deserts}$.
explanation: Despite being in the frozen continent, these valleys see almost no precipitation due to katabatic winds.

text: The $\textbf{Strait of Gibraltar}$ is the only natural link between the $\textbf{Atlantic Ocean}$ and the $\textbf{Mediterranean Sea}$.
explanation: It separates Europe (Spain) from Africa (Morocco) by just 14.3 km at its narrowest point.

text: The height of $\textbf{Mount Everest}$ was a topic of study in 2015 following the Nepal earthquake, to see if the mountain had $\textbf{Shrunk}$.
explanation: Satellite data initially suggested a slight decrease in height, though later surveys confirmed it remains the tallest peak.

text: The $\textbf{Amazon River}$ is the largest river by $\textbf{Discharge Volume}$ of water in the world, flowing through South America.
explanation: It accounts for approximately 20% of the world's total river flow to the oceans.

text: The $\textbf{Aral Sea}$, located between $\textbf{Kazakhstan}$ and $\textbf{Uzbekistan}$, has largely disappeared due to Soviet-era irrigation projects.
explanation: Once the fourth-largest lake in the world, it is now a fraction of its former size.

text: The region of $\textbf{Patagonia}$ is located at the southern end of South America, shared by $\textbf{Argentina}$ and $\textbf{Chile}$.
explanation: It is known for its dramatic mountain peaks, glaciers, and steppe-like plains.

text: The $\textbf{Dead Sea}$ is the lowest point on Earth's land surface, located on the border between $\textbf{Jordan}$, Israel, and the West Bank.
explanation: Its shores are about 430 meters below sea level and it is hypersaline.

text: The $\textbf{Gobi Desert}$ is a vast rain shadow desert formed by the $\textbf{Himalaya}$ mountains blocking rain-carrying clouds from the Indian Ocean.
explanation: It covers parts of northern and northwestern China and southern Mongolia.

text: The city of $\textbf{Istanbul}$ in $\textbf{Turkey}$ is the only major city in the world located on two $\textbf{Continents}$.
explanation: It spans Europe and Asia, divided by the Bosphorus Strait.

text: The $\textbf{Panama Canal}$ expansion project, aimed at accommodating larger 'New Panamax' ships, was nearing completion in 2015.
explanation: The expansion added a third set of locks to the canal, doubling its capacity.

text: The $\textbf{Crimean Peninsula}$ is separated from the Russian mainland by the $\textbf{Kerch Strait}$, where a major bridge construction began in 2015.
explanation: The bridge connects the Taman Peninsula of Krasnodar Krai to the Kerch Peninsula of Crimea.

text: The $\textbf{Sentinelese}$ people inhabit North Sentinel Island in the $\textbf{Andaman Islands}$, refusing all contact with the outside world.
explanation: They are considered one of the last uncontacted peoples, protected by Indian law.

text: The $\textbf{Svalbard Global Seed Vault}$ is located on the island of Spitsbergen in $\textbf{Norway}$, designed to preserve crop diversity.
explanation: Located deep inside a mountain in the Arctic circle, it is often called the 'Doomsday Vault'.

text: The $\textbf{Ngorongoro Crater}$ in $\textbf{Tanzania}$ is the world's largest inactive, intact, and unfilled volcanic $\textbf{Caldera}$.
explanation: It forms a self-contained ecosystem with a high density of wildlife.

text: The $\textbf{Lake Baikal}$ in $\textbf{Siberia}$ is the world's deepest lake and contains about 20% of the world's unfrozen freshwater.
explanation: It is home to thousands of species of plants and animals, many of which exist nowhere else.

text: The $\textbf{Murray-Darling Basin}$ is the agricultural heartland of $\textbf{Australia}$, which faced severe drought conditions around 2015.
explanation: It covers one-seventh of the Australian continent and is vital for irrigation.

text: The ancient city of $\textbf{Timbuktu}$, located in $\textbf{Mali}$, sits on the southern edge of the $\textbf{Sahara Desert}$.
explanation: Historically a center of trade and learning, it is threatened by desertification.
